full_judgment: 28. The Indian supreme court observed; "There can be no doubt that to be a Court, the person or persons who constitute it, must be entrusted with judicial functions, that is, of deciding litigated questions according to law. However, by argument between the parties, arbitrators may be called ups to exercise judicial powers and dear a dispute according to law but that would not make the arbitrators a Court. It appears to me that before a person or persons can be said to constitute a Court, it must be held that they derive their powers from the state and exercise the judicial powers of the state." (Maloyan and Bharat Bank Ltd. -v-Employees of Bharat Bank Ltd., AIR 1950 SC 188).
